question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for stimulating the growth and branching of the ductal system during pregnancy?
explanation: Estrogen drives the development and branching of the milk ducts, while progesterone works on the alveolar glands. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T2#BMP212_U4_T2_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of the oily secretions from the Montgomery glands on the areola?

options.A: Anchoring the baby's tongue during a feed
options.C: Providing extra protein to the baby

explanation: The Montgomery glands secrete a protective substance that keeps the nipple skin healthy and guards against cracking during frequent feeds. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T2#BMP212_U4_T2_h1)

question: Which hormone directly triggers the contraction of myoepithelial cells to cause the milk ejection reflex?
explanation: Oxytocin travels to the breast and causes the tiny muscles around the milk glands to squeeze milk into the ducts. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T2#BMP212_U4_T2_h2)

question: Why does milk production not happen in large amounts during pregnancy despite high prolactin levels?

options.A: High progesterone levels block prolactin's action
options.C: The infant has not yet stimulated the nipple
options.D: The alveoli are not yet formed until birth

explanation: Circulating placental progesterone keeps milk production suppressed until the placenta is delivered at birth. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T2#BMP212_U4_T2_h2)

question: What is the primary immunological benefit of colostrum for a newborn baby?
explanation: Colostrum is packed with antibodies like secretory IgA that line the baby's gut to prevent harmful germs from invading. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T2#BMP212_U4_T2_h3)

question: How does foremilk differ fundamentally from hindmilk within a single feed of mature milk?

options.A: Foremilk is higher in water content, while hindmilk is higher in fat content
options.B: Foremilk is produced at night, while hindmilk is produced during daylight feeds
options.C: Foremilk contains all the protein, while hindmilk contains only simple sugars
options.D: Foremilk is thick and yellow, while hindmilk is thin and clear

explanation: The milk at the start of a feed quenches thirst, while the milk at the end contains rich fats that satisfy the baby's hunger. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T2#BMP212_U4_T2_h3)

question: A postpartum mother complains of severe nipple pain and shows linear abrasions on her nipples. What is the most appropriate initial assessment to make?

options.A: Check the mother's temperature for signs of systemic infection
options.B: Prescribe an oral antifungal medication for suspected thrush
options.C: Advise the mother to stop breastfeeding for forty-eight hours
options.D: Observe the baby's latch and positioning at the breast

explanation: Nipple pain and trauma are almost always caused by poor attachment, making observation of the latch the essential first step. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T2#BMP212_U4_T2_h4)

question: Which visual sign indicates a correct, deep attachment during breastfeeding?

options.A: The mother feeling a sharp pinching sensation during sucking
options.B: The baby's cheeks appearing hollow and sucked inward
options.C: More areola visible above the baby's top lip than below
options.D: The baby's head turned to the side while the body faces upward

explanation: A deep latch requires taking a large mouthful of breast tissue from underneath, leaving more areola visible on top. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T2#BMP212_U4_T2_h4)

question: Which clinical feature helps distinguish mastitis from simple breast engorgement?

options.B: Tenderness when the baby begins to suck

explanation: Mastitis involves systemic signs like fever and chills, whereas engorgement and blocked ducts generally do not cause systemic illness. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T2#BMP212_U4_T2_h5)

question: Why is it important for a mother with mastitis to continue removing milk from the affected breast?

options.A: Breastmilk becomes toxic to the baby if it is allowed to stay in the gland
options.B: Stopping removal worsens stasis and increases the risk of abscess formation
options.C: Emptying the breast prevents the baby from catching the mother's infection
options.D: Prolactin levels will drop permanently if one feed is missed

explanation: Continuing to empty the breast prevents milk stasis from worsening and helps clear the infection alongside treatment. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T2#BMP212_U4_T2_h5)

question: Why is expressed breastmilk especially critical for the management of preterm infants in the neonatal unit?

options.A: Preterm infants cannot tolerate artificial milk formulas under any clinical circumstances
options.B: It provides specialized immunological protection and is easier for their immature gut to digest
options.C: It contains higher amounts of water to prevent dehydration caused by radiant warmers
options.D: Expressed milk eliminates the need for any vitamin or mineral supplementation

explanation: Preterm infants have fragile digestive systems and benefit immensely from the protective properties and easy digestibility of human milk. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T2#BMP212_U4_T2_h6)

question: What is the recommended initial action when a breastfeeding mother is prescribed a new medication?

options.A: Advise the mother to permanently wean her baby immediately
options.B: Switch the baby to full formula feeding without checking guidelines
options.C: Tell her to discard all expressed milk for the next two weeks
options.D: Consult a verified reference guide on drug safety during lactation

explanation: Most medications are safe during breastfeeding, so midwives must check reliable drug reference sources rather than automatically stopping breastfeeding. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T2#BMP212_U4_T2_h6)
